front_blocks.md: Why must nitric acid (not hydrochloric acid) be used when testing for halide ions?

back_blocks.md: Nitric acid is used instead of hydrochloric acid because hydrochloric acid contains **chloride ions** (Cl<sup>-</sup>), which would react with silver nitrate to produce a false white precipitate. Using **nitric acid** avoids this interference, giving an accurate result.

front_blocks.md: What are the two types of test that can be used to identify water?

back_blocks.md: Water can be identified by a **chemical test** and a **physical test**. The chemical test uses anhydrous copper(II) sulfate, while the physical test checks the **boiling point** of the liquid.

front_blocks.md: Why is checking the boiling point a physical test for the purity of water?

back_blocks.md: Pure water boils at exactly **100 °C**. By heating a sample and measuring its **boiling point**, you can check whether it is pure — impurities raise the boiling point above 100 °C, indicating the water is not pure.
